title: An affine span has a finite-stage model with both target families fixed
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $B$ and projections $p_i:B\to S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$, affine schemes $P_0,Q_0$ of finite presentation over $S_{i_0}$, and an affine scheme $U$ of finite presentation over $B$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge i_0$ put $P_i=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $Q_i=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $P_B=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}B$, and $Q_B=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Given arbitrary $B$-morphisms $a:U\to P_B$ and $c:U\to Q_B$, there exist $r\ge i_0$, an affine scheme $V_r$ of finite presentation over $S_r$, $S_r$-morphisms $\alpha_r:V_r\to P_r$, $\beta_r:V_r\to Q_r$, and a $B$-isomorphism $e_r:V_r\times_{S_r}B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ such that $\alpha_{r,B}=a\circ e_r$ and $\beta_{r,B}=c\circ e_r$. Here $\alpha_{r,B},\beta_{r,B}$ are the actual base changes of the two stage arrows, with targets identified with $P_B,Q_B$ by the unique iterated-fibre-product isomorphisms preserving projections. No etaleness or point is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (1),(2), and Tag 01ZN, lemma-descend-affine-finite-presentation; simultaneous fixed-target affine-span construction in More on Morphisms Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, finite-stage span paragraph.

proof.text: All $S_i$ and $U$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Every transition map $S_j\to S_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. We may restrict the index set to $I_{\ge i_0}$ without changing the limit: a cone on this tail extends to an index $i$ by choosing $k\ge i,i_0$ and composing its $k$-leg with $S_k\to S_i$. Two choices agree after passing to a common upper bound, and the extended cone is unique. Thus the universal property of the given limit $B$ is also the limit property for the tail. This also proves the same assertion for each later tail used below.

Apply part (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $U\to B$ over this tail. It gives $j\ge i_0$, a finitely presented $S_j$-scheme $W_j$, and a $B$-isomorphism $e_j:(W_j)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$. The source $W_j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since its structure map is of finite presentation and $S_j$ is qcqs. By (3), every later base change remains finitely presented. In particular the prescribed $P_j,Q_j$, and all their later base changes, are of finite presentation.

The limit structure map $(W_j)_B\to B$ is affine: $e_j$ identifies its source with the affine scheme $U$, and $B$ is affine by the final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] applies. Use [lem-weil-pbc-descend-affine] with $X_j=W_j$, $Y_j=S_j$ and the tail based at $j$. Its qcqs hypotheses were verified above. There is $k\ge j$ for which $V_k:=W_j\times_{S_j}S_k\to S_k$ is affine. Since $S_k$ is affine, (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $V_k$ affine. It is finitely presented by base-change permanence. The unique projection-preserving iterated-pullback isomorphism of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $e_k:(V_k)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ by composing with $e_j$.

Put $a_k=a\circ e_k:(V_k)_B\to P_B$. Apply part (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the fixed finitely presented $S_k$-models $V_k$ and $P_k$. It gives $l\ge k$ and an $S_l$-map $\alpha_l:V_l\to P_l$, where $V_l=V_k\times_{S_k}S_l$, whose base change is $a_k$. Here and below each target $(P_k)_{S_l}$ is identified with the actual prescribed $P_l$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], preserving both projections. By (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $V_l$ and $Q_l$ are finitely presented. Apply part (2) again to these fixed models and $c\circ e_l:(V_l)_B\to Q_B$, where $e_l=e_k\circ\theta_l$ and $\theta_l:(V_l)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}(V_k)_B$ preserves projections. It gives $r\ge l$ and $\beta_r:V_r\to Q_r$ whose base change is $c\circ e_l$. Define $\alpha_r$ as the actual base change of $\alpha_l$ along $S_r\to S_l$, followed by the projection-preserving target comparison to $P_r$.

The scheme $V_r=V_l\times_{S_l}S_r$ is affine: $V_k\to S_k$ was affine, and (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] apply to each subsequent base change over the affine bases $S_l,S_r$. Its structure map is finitely presented by (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

Let $\theta_{rl}:(V_r)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}(V_l)_B$ be the iterated-fibre-product comparison and set $e_r=e_l\circ\theta_{rl}$. To verify the arrows, [def-pc-fibre-product] characterizes the base change of $\alpha_l$ by its projection to $P_l$ and its structure map to $B$. Composing these projections through either iterated pullback gives the same two maps. Uniqueness therefore gives $\alpha_{r,B}=\alpha_{l,B}\circ\theta_{rl}=a\circ e_l\circ\theta_{rl}=a\circ e_r$. The equality supplied for $\beta_r$ similarly reads $\beta_{r,B}=c\circ e_l\circ\theta_{rl}=c\circ e_r$. The target comparisons to $P_B,Q_B$ have the same projection characterization, so these equations concern the actual base changes required in the statement. Finally $r\ge l\ge k\ge j\ge i_0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q23-d549f6d1a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Ordinary one-level split of an unsplit node with no repair note: no new nodes, and the statement, stmt_deps and provenance are unchanged. Checked against Stacks more-morphisms.tex:11144 (lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre). Its finite-stage paragraph ('By Limits lemma-descend-finite-presentation ... diagram X_i <- U_i -> Y_i') is exactly this item without the étale/point refinement. Step 1: the affine bases are qcqs, the transition maps are affine (01SH), and the tail I>=i0 has the same limit B (elementary, correct). Step 2: thm-pd-spreading-out (1) gives a finitely presented model W_j, which is qcqs by qcqs-permanence (2); clause (3) gives finite presentation of P_j and Q_j. Step 3: B is affine by the final clause of lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition, and W_B is isomorphic to U, which is affine, so W_B->B is affine. lem-weil-pbc-descend-affine (01ZN) applies with X0=W_j, Y0=S_j; its qcqs hypotheses are verified, and it does not need f to be finitely presented. Affine-permanence (2) then makes V_k affine. Step 4: spreading-out (2) is used twice on fixed finitely presented models; the first arrow is pulled back to the second arrow's stage, and the targets are identified with P_B and Q_B by the canonical projection-preserving isomorphisms. Steps 5-6 (affineness and the equations alpha_{r,B}=a∘e_r, beta_{r,B}=c∘e_r via fibre-product uniqueness) are correct. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Route: sk-thm-p1 is on the transitive route of sk-i-curve-zero, and thm-pd-spreading-out is slopmaster2-closed, so it is a tool. The three declared tool_uses are on-route Mathlib leaves (unnecessary, harmless). Duplicates: lem-weil-pbc-finite-diagram-lift-of-models gives neither source affineness nor canonical target identification; the family-descent node handles objects only. Edge cases checked: U empty, one-element I, non-injective transitions, arrows descending at unrelated stages. Advisory: the inherited statement cites def-weil-pbc-category-colimit for a limit (duality, not new here). No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_fixedFamily_affine_span_model {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsAffine (D.obj i)] (L : Cone D) (hL : IsLimit L) (i₀ : I) (P₀ Q₀ : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine P₀] [IsAffine Q₀] (fP : P₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀)) (fQ : Q₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀)) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fP] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fQ] (U : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine U] (fU : U ⟶ L.pt) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fU] (a : U ⟶ pullback fP (L.π.app (op i₀))) (c : U ⟶ pullback fQ (L.π.app (op i₀))) (ha : a ≫ pullback.snd fP (L.π.app (op i₀)) = fU) (hc : c ≫ pullback.snd fQ (L.π.app (op i₀)) = fU) : ∃ (r : I) (hr : i₀ ≤ r) (V : Scheme.{u}) (fV : V ⟶ D.obj (op r)), IsAffine V ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation fV ∧ ∃ (α : V ⟶ pullback fP (D.map (homOfLE hr).op)) (β : V ⟶ pullback fQ (D.map (homOfLE hr).op)), α ≫ pullback.snd fP (D.map (homOfLE hr).op) = fV ∧ β ≫ pullback.snd fQ (D.map (homOfLE hr).op) = fV ∧ ∃ e : pullback fV (L.π.app (op r)) ≅ U, e.hom ≫ fU = pullback.snd fV (L.π.app (op r)) ∧ e.hom ≫ a ≫ pullback.fst fP (L.π.app (op i₀)) = pullback.fst fV (L.π.app (op r)) ≫ α ≫ pullback.fst fP (D.map (homOfLE hr).op) ∧ e.hom ≫ c ≫ pullback.fst fQ (L.π.app (op i₀)) = pullback.fst fV (L.π.app (op r)) ≫ β ≫ pullback.fst fQ (D.map (homOfLE hr).op)
